steps.text: Place chicken and salsa in the slow cooker the night before you want to eat this chili. Season with garlic powder, cumin, chili powder, salt, and pepper. Cook on Low for 6 to 8 hours.
About 3 to 4 hours before you want to eat, remove chicken to a cutting board and shred with 2 forks. Return meat to the slow cooker.
Stir in pinto beans and corn. Simmer until ready to serve.

raw_recipe.headline: Chicken and Corn Chili
raw_recipe.description: This chicken and corn chili is simmered in a slow cooker with pinto beans and flavored with salsa, cumin, and chili powder for a comforting dish.
raw_recipe.name: Chicken and Corn Chili

recipeInstructions.text: Place chicken and salsa in the slow cooker the night before you want to eat this chili. Season with garlic powder, cumin, chili powder, salt, and pepper. Cook on Low for 6 to 8 hours.
About 3 to 4 hours before you want to eat, remove chicken to a cutting board and shred with 2 forks. Return meat to the slow cooker.
Stir in pinto beans and corn. Simmer until ready to serve.

review.reviewBody: The first person to taste this chili asked for the recipe! I did make the following changes and additions...3 chicken breasts instead of 4, 1 can of diced green chilis, 2 teaspoons fresh garlic instead of the garlic powder, 16 ounce can of diced tomatoes, and 2 teaspoons sugar to cut the acidity of the tomatoes. OTHERWISE, this was a great recipe and will be added to my winter repertoire! Thanks.

This recipe has become a staple in my house. I find that simply throwing it all in together in one step turns out just as good. I cook on low for 8 hours, and then just stir. The chicken just falls apart. I add some cayenne for a kick. Very yummy.

Like others, I added a can of green chiles and used black beans (personal preference). For sake of time, I used a can of white chicken breast in water...tasted great, wouldn't have known the difference. Served with cheese, sour cream and avocado. Leftovers will be tacos. Thanks!

Great healthy chili recipe. I made it for Superbowl Sunday and it was a hit. Changes to the recipe: I used 3 boneless chicken breasts and that was plenty. As other reviews did, I added a can of diced green chili peppers, 1 whole fresh jalapeño pepper, and fresh garlic and a can of small diced tomatoes with jalapeños. I doubled the spices and used small red kidney beans. I cooked the chicken salsa and minced tomatoes on low for about 6 hours (no need to do this overnight) on low and then added 16 oz bag of defrosted frozen corn and the beans and cooked on low for another two hours. I may add another fresh jalapeño pepper the next time.

I give this recipe 5 stars because I have been making it for almost 10 years now & have only made minor tweaks. It is tasty, easily editable, can easily feed more if you have surprise guests (just add more beans & corn, no one really notices) and takes about 5 minutes to make. What is not to like? I have made these changes over the years - the night before I follow the recipe and I add a can of rotel, and few splashes of hot sauce. Day of I cook it up but just throw in a bag of frozen corn & a can of beans; I find you don't need mexican corn if you use the rotel, and I almost always have everything on hand except mexi-corn. Thank you Sarah Jane for a great recipe!

Very Tasty. I used 1 container of fresh hot salsa, 1/2 jar mild salsa, 1 can of mild green chilis. I cooked everything for 7 hours, shredded the chicken and added a can of rotel, frozen corn, pinto and black beans (cooked from dried beans instead of a can). Then I cooked the chili for another 4 hours. This is very easy.

I’ve made this recipe a few times now. I cooked the chicken on high for 4 hrs- then added about 3/4 cup chicken broth, as this recipe has a tendency to not have enough liquid. Don’t drain the beans or corn! Serve with your favorite toppings. Enjoy!

My favorite eeeeasy dish and my go-to for football gatherings and bring-along to parties. A winner. People stalk me down at those events to ask for the recipe. I always keep on hand frozen bagged *sweet white corn just in case. Always use sweet white corn, not Mexican style. I add whatever beans or spices I have on hand to substitute. However one thing I stick with for sure is *Pace Picante Sauce. Have tried several types of salsa, Pace works the best for me. One time I didn't have chicken broth, which a lot of these recipes ask, and it was fine. Just made sure I did not drain the canned items. Easy to adjust the amount of chicken too. When the I often get lazy and don't measure, think it would be hard to screw this up. We just got a Yedi Insta-Pot so will try it in that next. Happy winter cooking friends!

This is great. Of course I changed a lot of things, most importantly, I didn't use a slow cooker. I used a 3 lb rotisserie chicken (cooked already) from BJs and just shredded it. I used the red beans, 2 cans of enchilada sauce, one can of tomatoes with green chilils and a "natural" salsa from the store. (I took a lot of ideas from the people below.) I also added chicken stock. I used frozen corn instead of canned (bleh) I didnt double the spices, but you could if you like an extra kick. It's REALLY GOOD, serve with grated cheese and a dollop of sour cream and Frito scoops for dipping! YUM

I make this all the time but I realized I might have been reading the recipe wrong because the chicken is usually over cooked and the overall recipe is a bit dry. This time I added some Chicken broth after I shredded the chicken and that helped. I usually cook it for 6 hours then shred it and cook another 3. Next time I will cook it for 4 or 5 hours, then shred it and continue cooking another 3. I also, like many others add black beans to this. I serve it with shredded cheddar cheese and sour cream and sometimes Triscuits. Great recipe and super easy to make

I gave this recipe four stars out of 5, mainly because while it had an excellent taste, it didn't have the consistency of chili. It was way too thick. But, not wanting to give up on a great taste, I modified it a little and used it as a filling for enchiladas. I rolled about a two tablespoons of the mixture plus a tablespoon or so of shredded jack cheese into each corn tortilla, ending up with a full 12 enchiladas in a 9 x 13 pan. Then I topped in with a can of enchilada sauce and some more cheese, baked at a 350 degree oven for 30 minutes. Delicious! Plus there was a good amount of chili left over for freezing and using another night.
An easy chili recipe and a nice twist using chicken!

I’m missing something to this recipe that is being raved about. The salsa does not prove de enough liquid for this to be chili. I think there is an ingredient missing. I added a can of crushed tomatoes and half of a box of chicken broth to get it to a chili consistency. I haven’t tasted it yet. Can someone please explain where the liquid is supposed to come from?
I can usually eat about anything, so I don't know why, to me, it taste so bad. I made it just as directed. Maybe it is the salsa I used.
I made this but used my homemade salsa an used black beans instead of pinto beans so good. I don't like pinto beans .
Super easy and tasty, I have been making it regularly for years. I usually add a can of black beans to make it go a little longer

I read through some of the complaints so I made sure to address some of those with how I managed to make it not dry or bland! I plan on also adding cheese and sour cream as a topping. Very easy to make. I added a small can of tomato sauce to the salsa for extra liquid/ flavor Then I put the the salsa, seasoning & 2 large chicken breast (as oposed to 4) In the crock pot on high for 2.5 hours. Then I lightly shredded the chicken & added the corn (not drained) & the pinto beans (75% drained) and let cook for the remaining 2 hours. I was a bit more generous with my seasonings! Make sure you get the correct size of salsa (16 oz) & the same size pinto beans / corn sizes to be sure you have the right consistency. I opted for the chunky salsa so it would be less liquidy!
